title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, Customer Requirements Library
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended reference architectures, packaging guidance, day-2 operational runbooks, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). Target audience: Solutions Engineers, Platform Engineers, SRE, and Customer Success teams supporting private deployments.

Goals
- Provide repeatable, supportable deployment patterns for VPC and on-prem customers.
- Define operational playbooks for day-2 activities (monitoring, scaling, safe restarts, incident triage).
- Standardize upgrade and rollback procedures to minimize downtime and data loss.
- Maintain a customer requirements library to accelerate scoping and contracts.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood Private control plane + on-prem inference nodes and VPC-connected deployments.
- Excludes hosted (public) API operations and Dedicated managed fleet details.

Quick links
- Reference architectures (section A)
- Packaging & installation (section B)
- Day-2 ops checklist & runbook (section C)
- Upgrade & rollback (section D)
- Customer requirements library (section E)

A. Reference architectures
Purpose: show recommended network layouts, HA topology, and sizing guidance for common customer profiles.

A.1. Small (POC) – Single-region VPC
- Use a single VPC with two private subnets across two AZs.
- Control plane components (customer-managed or Redwood-hosted control plane) in private subnets with NAT for outbound updates.
- Inference nodes in an autoscaling node group with minimum 1, max 3 GPUs.
- Recommended components and ports:
  - Load balancer (internal NLB) -> 443 to ingress agents
  - Control plane API -> 8443 (internal)
  - KV cache / persistence (optional) -> PostgreSQL 5432 (private)
- Sizing guidance: 1-3 A100/RTX6000-equivalent GPUs for small POC.

A.2. Production (Multi-AZ hybrid)
- Control plane placed in customer-managed VPC or Redwood Private control plane (per contract).
- Separate subnet pools for control, inference, storage, and management.
- Dedicated GPU pools by tier (standard, high-throughput).
- Cross-AZ replicas for stateful services (postgres, redis).
- Optional on-prem inference nodes connected over VPN/Direct Connect for data residency and latency-sensitive workloads.

A.3. Air-gapped on-prem
- Two-tier architecture: management plane (on isolated management network) + inference rack(s).
- Use on-prem package with offline install artifacts and optional airgap broker for updates.
- On-prem HSM/KMS integration guidance (see packaging section).

Architecture decision matrix (summary)
| Requirement | Pattern | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Low latency, single tenant | On-prem GPU rack | Customer owns hardware, best latency |
| Regulated data | VPC + Private control plane | Combine VPC networking controls and audit logs |
| Fast scale | Cloud VPC + Dedicated GPU pool | Autoscaling and burst capacity |

B. Packaging & installation
B.1. Packaging formats
- VPC deployment: Helm charts for Kubernetes (EKS/GKE/AKS) + Terraform modules for networking.
- On-prem: OCI images + tarball installer and systemd-managed services; optional k3s/rook for smaller footprints.
- Offline package includes: container images (sha256 list), Helm charts, CRDs, configuration templates, and a signed manifest.

B.2. Installation checklist (example)
1. Validate customer network: CIDR, peering/VPN, NAT gateways, outbound proxy rules.
2. Provision base infra: Kubernetes cluster (version constraint documented), node pools, network policies.
3. Apply CA and TLS certs: provide CSR guidance and recommended CNs.
4. Install control plane components: database, object store connector (S3-compatible), control api, ingress.
5. Deploy inference runtime: GPU device plugin, runtime operator, model store.
6. Smoke tests: curl health endpoints, run sample inference workload, verify metrics exported to configured monitoring endpoint.

Example Helm override (snippet):
```yaml
replicaCount: 3
image:
  registry: <private-registry>
  pullSecret: redwood-pull-secret
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
nodeSelector:
  gpu: "true"
autoscaling:
  enabled: true
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 10
```

B.3. Secrets & key management
- Integrations: AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, or on-prem HSM.
- Secrets must be mounted via CSI or provided through a secrets operator; avoid in-cluster plaintext files.
- Rotation: document key rotation window with customer (90 days recommended for high-security customers).

C. Day-2 operations: runbooks and playbooks
C.1. Runbook: scaling an inference pool
1. Verify current utilization: check per-GPU GPU_utilization%, queue latency, and token throughput.
2. If sustained GPU_util > 75% for 10+ mins, plan scale event.
3. Scale via k8s autoscaling or adjust node group desired count.
4. Monitor for warm-up latency increase (KV cache cold misses).
5. If errors rate increases >5% over baseline, revert scale and open incident.

C.2. Routine health checks (daily)
- Control plane health endpoints: /health, /ready
- Database replication lag: <2s goal for active clustering
- Disk usage: alert when any disk >70% used
- GPU metrics: memory pressure, power usage, temperature thresholds (per vendor)

C.3. Incident triage (short)
- Priority levels: P1 (service down), P2 (degraded latency/errors), P3 (nonblocking).
- For P1: page oncall, run immediate rollback (if caused by recent change), switch to fallback model variant, and activate traffic routing policy.
- For P2: collect logs, begin investigation, enable increased tracing for 10m windows, consult serving-runtime team.

D. Upgrade and rollback procedures
D.1. Principles
- Upgrades should be staged (canary -> partial -> full).
- Always have a tested rollback path that is faster than the forward upgrade in case of P1.
- Preserve model artifacts and KV caches when safe; document breaking migrations.

D.2. Kubernetes-based upgrade (control plane)
1. Create a canary namespace (or label subset of replicas) and apply new Helm chart with image tag.
2. Run integration smoke tests for model load, generation sanity, metrics export, and auth flows.
3. Monitor for 15-30 minutes. If no regressions, promote to 25%, then 50%, then 100% using traffic shaping.
4. When promoting, apply DB migrations only after canary success and keep migrations backward-compatible if possible.

D.3. Rollback steps (fast path)
1. If canary fails: immediately scale canary down and delete canary deployment.
2. If global failure: revert Helm release to previous chart revision using helm rollback <release> <revision>.
3. If DB migration caused failure: restore DB snapshot (follow DB restore runbook) and revert application.
4. Post-incident: run regression tests, create a postmortem, and update the upgrade checklist.

E. Customer requirements library
E.1. Common questions to capture during scoping
- Network topology: Can customer provide VPC peering/Direct Connect or require site-to-site VPN?
- Compliance: required certifications (SOC2, ISO27001, HIPAA).
- Data residency: allowed regions, retention windows, and encryption at rest requirements.
- Hardware: preferred GPU vendors, procurement timelines, power/cooling constraints for on-prem.
- High availability: RTO/RPO expectations and required SLA tiers.

E.2. Minimum information checklist (deliverable during sales handoff)
- Administrative contacts and escalation path
- Network diagrams and CIDR ranges
- Service account keys and registry access plan
- Expected baseline token throughput and latency SLOs
- Maintenance windows and blackout periods

F. Templates and checklists
- Pre-deployment checklist (network, certs, quotas)
- Post-deployment verification checklist (end-to-end smoke tests)
- Upgrade runbook checklist (canary targets, metrics to watch, rollback triggers)

Ownership & escalation
- Deployment owner: Solutions Engineering (primary) + Customer Success (engagement).
- Operational ownership: Customer SRE (day-2) with Redwood oncall escalation for platform issues.
- Escalation matrix: list named contacts (on internal page).

SLOs & Monitoring recommendations
- Control plane API: p99 latency <120ms (internal target), availability 99.95% for enterprise SLA customers.
- Inference request p95 latency target depends on model class; record targets in customer agreement.
- Recommended monitoring stack: Prometheus for metrics, Grafana dashboards, Loki for logs. Export to customer SIEM where required.

```bash
# basic health
curl -sfS https://internal-controlplane.local/health || exit 1
# quick generation test
curl -sS -X POST https://internal-ingress.local/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":8}' | jq
```
